York, 7 November 2026. Today, residents of York can expect a mild day with light rain forecast throughout. Afternoon temperatures are poised to reach a maximum of 10°C, while the minimum may drop to around 7°C. The atmosphere is predicted to remain quite humid, registering at about 96%. As such, locals should prepare for a damp day with minimal sunshine.
Despite the rain, today's weather is set to be relatively mild, with the possibility of drizzle enhancing the overall chill in the air. Residents can anticipate a generally overcast day, with rain likely early in the morning and persisting into late afternoon.
York Weather Today
Today's weather will feature temperatures peaking at 10°C during the afternoon and dipping to a low of approximately 7°C by nightfall. The humidity level will be quite high, at around 96%, which may contribute to a damp feeling in the air. As for precipitation, there is a 10% chance of rain, meaning occasional light rain may occur, but it is not expected to be significant.
Expect the skies to be predominantly cloudy, with some bursts of light rain throughout the day. Winds will be relatively calm, further contributing to an overall dull feeling in the atmosphere.
While the rain isn't expected to be heavy, those heading outdoors might experience brief showers that could make for a soggy experience.
Prepare for a Damp Day
With light rain expected, residents should consider carrying an umbrella and wearing water-resistant footwear if they plan to step outside. It's advisable to dress in layers, as the temperature will be cool, particularly in the morning and evening. Those with outdoor plans might want to adjust their activities to accommodate for the likelihood of intermittent rain.
If you are commuting, factor in additional time, especially if the rain picks up. It's a good day for indoor activities or errands that require minimal outdoor exposure. The rain is not anticipated to be severe, but it might disrupt plans for outdoor outings or events.

Looking ahead, the next seven days indicate a range of weather conditions for York, with temperatures generally fluctuating between 2°C and 10°C. Expect predominantly cloudy conditions on several days, but sunny intervals could bring some brightness midweek.
Sunday will see temperatures drop to a cooler 3°C in the morning, warming only slightly throughout the day. Following this, residents can anticipate intermittent sunshine on Monday and Tuesday, which should offer milder weather. The coolest day appears to be next Saturday with a high of just 7°C.
Overall, York will experience a mix of chilly, overcast stretches interspersed with sunny periods over the next week, so residents are encouraged to plan accordingly.

articles.title: More than 1,100 people affected as record November rains put northern Peru under red alert - Latin Times

articles.full_text:
Peru's meteorological agency SENAMHI has extended a red alert for extreme rainfall across Tumbes and Piura through Sunday, November 8, projecting localized accumulations above 100 millimeters and wind gusts near 40 km/h.
The storm system has already displaced 324 residents and affected 808 more across Tumbes, leaving 109 homes uninhabitable and triggering six flash-flood-prone gullies known as quebradas.
Experts warn this outbreak marks the opening of a prolonged rainy season driven by El Niño Costero, which forecasters expect to sustain above-normal precipitation across Peru's northern coast through early 2027.
The pace at which rain is falling on northern Peru this November is not simply unusual — in Tumbes, it is rewriting the historical record. Peru's meteorological agency, the Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología (SENAMHI), has placed 11 provinces across Tumbes and Piura under red alert, with storm conditions projected to persist through Sunday, November 8, 2026. Officials warn that localized rainfall totals in Tumbes could surpass 100 millimeters before the system passes through.
A Record-Breaking Start to November
The numbers coming out of Tumbes are striking. By November 5, rainfall accumulated during the first five days of the month had reached values as much as 100 times above the region's average climatological totals for the entire month — figures that exceeded records logged even during confirmed El Niño years. The worst single-event measurement came from the district of San Jacinto, where the village of Rica Playa recorded 112.5 liters per square meter. SENAMHI specialist Javier Chiong had already warned that specific localities in Piura and Tumbes could surpass 100 millimeters per episode depending on atmospheric conditions — a threshold now confirmed at multiple monitoring stations.
Eleven Provinces on Maximum Threat Level
Notice No. 307-2026, issued by SENAMHI on November 3, placed 605 districts across 26 regions on a 24-hour alert and identified the northern coast as the zone of most extreme risk. Eleven provinces remain under red-level monitoring: three in Tumbes — Contralmirante Villar, Tumbes and Zarumilla — and eight in Piura, including Ayabaca, Huancabamba, Morropón, Sullana and Talara, among others. The forecast includes sustained wind gusts near 40 kilometers per hour and electrical storm activity in both regions, with hail possible at elevations above 2,800 meters.
324 Displaced, 109 Homes Uninhabitable
The human cost is already substantial. Figures from the Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN) confirm that 324 residents have been displaced and 808 more have been affected across Tumbes, with 109 dwellings declared structurally uninhabitable. Six quebradas — normally dry gullies that fill and overflow under heavy precipitation — submerged homes in the villages of Vaquería and Casa Blanqueada. The José Abelardo Quiñones technological institute in Tumbes city also sustained flooding. No fatalities have been reported as of this publication. The Housing Ministry, Tumbes Regional Government, Indeci and Army units have deployed pumps, heavy machinery and personnel to assist with drainage, road recovery and temporary shelters.
The meteorological context explains why November is behaving like the peak of the rainy season. El Niño Costero has driven sea surface temperatures off northern Peru's Pacific coastline to anomalous highs — SENAMHI measured approximately 26°C off Piura — feeding moisture into convective systems that would typically not develop at this time of year. The agency had been warning since June that the northern coast faced elevated rainfall probabilities beginning in November 2026, with peak intensity projected between December 2026 and March 2027. The rivers Tumbes, Piura and Chira have already registered sudden caudal spikes surpassing 100 percent above their historical daily averages for this date.
A Long Season Just Getting Started
What this weekend's red alert reveals is the opening chapter of a prolonged meteorological cycle. Regional and local authorities in Tumbes and Piura have been directed to accelerate coordination on flood management, drainage infrastructure and early warning protocols — especially along the historically vulnerable Tumbes and Chira river basins. For the more than 1,100 residents already affected, and the tens of thousands more in high-risk hydrological zones across both regions, the emergency systems activated since September are now being tested against the most intense November rains on record.
